subject: Next steps: DPA evidence & controller/processor mapping for BrightLedger
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Tremblay <sophie@brightledger.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: Post-call recap + immediate asks (DPA, SCC, evidence)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps:

- Your priorities: ensure data residency & contractual guarantees for EU customers, confirm GDPR roles for BrightLedger integrations, and evidence for security posture for procurement.
- Redwood status highlights we mentioned: hosted API with per-tenant routing, optional VPC/private deployment for regulated customers, SOC 2 Type II in progress (audit fieldwork scheduled Aug 2026), and standard DPA + SCC modules we can offer.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Please share the vendor security questionnaire you run internally (you indicated ~20 questions + a data-flow appendix).
2) Confirm whether BrightLedger will act as controller for end-customer data and whether you expect Redwood to be a sub-processor for any EU subsidiaries.

Attached is a draft DPA template with module options (Module A: standard EU SCCs + processor model; Module B: controller-to-controller variant for data co-processing scenarios). We flagged places where we need your legal team to confirm preferred module.

Next steps / timeline proposal:
- Sophie: send your questionnaire and any non-negotiable contract clauses by Tue 2026-07-20.
- Redwood (Ben/Marissa): we will complete the questionnaire responses and propose redlines to the DPA by Fri 2026-07-24.
- Legal sync (if needed): 30-minute call w/ BrightLedger GC to close outstanding role mapping.

Attachments: Draft_DPA_Redwood_vBrightLedger_20260714.docx (draft modules A/B).

Thanks — Jordan

--

Date: 2026-07-14T11:04:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + immediate asks (DPA, SCC, evidence)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear recap. Attaching the vendor questionnaire as requested. Two clarifications before we proceed:

1) Controller/processor: BrightLedger is the controller for customer account data; in a subset of integrations our EU subsidiary ingests raw PII and will want contractual assurances that Redwood acts as processor. We have one use case where data is enriched by our analytics team — that may be treated as joint-controller depending on the flow.

2) Evidence: Procurement wants a current SOC 2 report OR a documented remediation plan with timelines if a control is still in progress. You mentioned audit fieldwork in Aug — can you provide a short cover note about scope & expected delivery?

I've CC'd Alex (GC) for the DPA module decision — Alex, can you confirm whether BrightLedger will require controller-to-controller terms for the analytics enrichment flow or whether processor terms are acceptable?

Attached: BrightLedger_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (fillable).

Sophie Tremblay
Head of IT Operations, BrightLedger
sophie@brightledger.com | +44 20 7946 0821
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Tremblay <sophie@brightledger.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T10:22:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + immediate asks (DPA, SCC, evidence)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the questionnaire — we completed the first pass (see answers in the attached PDF export when we return). A few points on your two clarifications:

- SOC 2: Redwood completed readiness and controls design in Q1 2026, and fieldwork for Type II is scheduled for Aug 1-10. Expected report delivery is late Sept 2026. Procurement accepts interim evidence; we can provide: control matrix, summary of control tests performed so far, and our remediation tracker with target dates. Ill attach the summary doc to the response package.

- Controller/processor mapping: for the enrichment flow you described, we typically recommend the following:
  * If BrightLedger materially determines the purposes and means of enrichment (e.g., defines the enrichment models, retains direct rights over outputs), BrightLedger remains controller and Redwood acts as processor.
  * If both parties make joint decisions about purposes and means, we can accommodate a joint-controller addendum but it requires specific language and obligations in the DPA.

For speed, the pragmatic path is to sign the standard processor DPA (Module A) for the core integration and include a short joint-processing addendum for the analytics enrichment path. That minimizes procurement friction while preserving legal clarity.

I've attached: Redwood_Questionnaire_Response_20260715.pdf and a short SOC2_CoverNote_2026Q3.pdf.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Alex (GC): can you confirm preference by Mon 2026-07-20 so Jordan/Marissa can prepare redlines?
- If Alex prefers joint-controller terms, propose 30-min call Wed 2026-07-22.

Ben

--

Sophie / Alex —

Following up on Ben's materials. Alex, any quick call-out on whether BrightLedgers procurement would accept the SOC2 cover note + remediation tracker as interim evidence? If not, flag which controls (e.g., encryption key management, access reviews) they need explicit test evidence for.

If procurement is happy with interim evidence, Jordan/Redwood will:
- Finalize questionnaire responses and return by Fri 2026-07-17 (we accelerated).
- Produce DPA redlines for Module A + an optional short joint-processing addendum by Tue 2026-07-21.

If you prefer to fast-track: I can loop in our legal ops and schedule a short triage with Alex + Redwood counsel. Proposed slots: Tue 2026-07-21 09:00-09:30 or Wed 2026-07-22 14:00-14:30 (CEST). Let me know which works and I'll send calendar invite + DocuSign stub for the draft DPA.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this so BrightLedger can begin a pilot.

Jordan
